mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES remains below the prior four-week average while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, weekday trip chaining into shopping districts stays weak and RETAIL_REC falls further over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES staying at or below its current level and RESIDENTIAL staying at or above its current level.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in GROCERY_PHARM absorbs discretionary errands away from malls and restaurants, so when grocery visits stay above their recent norm, RETAIL_REC declines within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above 4 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not weaken within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM remains above 4 points for two straight weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES move up together, commuting and downtown circulation recover, increasing incidental retail exposure and pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both trend upward for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in PARKS after the late-summer leisure peak signals seasonal substitution back toward indoor shopping, so lower park activity should precede a rebound in RETAIL_REC over one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -5 points after having been above -10 points the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 days after PARKS drops through the stated threshold.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, simultaneous declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES reduce shopping trips more than any isolated category move, causing RETAIL_REC to fall over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall below their previous two-week averages by at least 2 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES drop below their prior two-week averages by the stated margin.

mechanism_narrative: A rising RESIDENTIAL share means more time spent at home and fewer discretionary outings, so continued residential upticks should translate into weaker RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over the next 14 days while RESIDENTIAL continues to rise relative to the current week.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL are both high, household time is reallocated to local necessities and at-home activity, which suppresses discretionary retail demand and lowers RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though both GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL remain above their recent averages.

mechanism_narrative: If retail mobility has already rebounded for a week while TRANSIT stays deeply negative, the rebound is travel-constrained rather than demand-led and should reverse within one week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC rises for one week while TRANSIT remains below -20 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues rising or stays above its current level over the next 7 days despite TRANSIT remaining below -20 points.
